result.summary: Report -rpcwhitelist denials as structured JSON-RPC errors instead of empty HTTP 403 responses. Introduce error codes RPC_METHOD_NOT_PERMITTED (-38) for refused method calls and RPC_REQUEST_NOT_EXECUTED (-39) for unexecuted calls in a rejected batch. Return HTTP 200 with an error object or array for JSON-RPC 2.0 and batch requests, while retaining HTTP 403 with an error payload for legacy 1.x requests.
result.problem: Requests refused by -rpcwhitelist return an empty HTTP 403 body. This violates documented JSON-RPC 2.0 behavior (which requires errors in HTTP 200 response bodies), causes bitcoin-cli over HTTP to show an uninformative 403 message, and breaks bitcoin-cli over IPC (-ipcconnect) with JSON type decoding errors because IPC receives only the body without HTTP status codes.
evidence: Identified in a private security audit of the IPC interface (ar-56) where bitcoin-cli -ipcconnect fails with a JSON type error on rejected calls.
Brings -rpcwhitelist error handling in line with JSON-RPC 2.0 behavior documented in #27101 and doc/JSON-RPC-interface.md.
result.scope_notes: Modifies HTTP RPC processing in src/httprpc.cpp and adds two RPCErrorCode enum entries in src/rpc/protocol.h.
result.changed_since_previous: Diff provided; no changes to commits or design relative to the previous version.
result.card: Bitcoin Core currently returns an empty HTTP 403 response when requests are refused by -rpcwhitelist, which leaves HTTP clients with vague errors and breaks bitcoin-cli over IPC with JSON decoding errors. This PR changes whitelist refusals to return standard JSON-RPC errors in the response body using new error codes RPC_METHOD_NOT_PERMITTED (-38) and RPC_REQUEST_NOT_EXECUTED (-39). JSON-RPC 2.0 single and batch requests now receive HTTP 200 responses with structured error objects, matching existing JSON-RPC 2.0 specifications. The defect was surfaced during a security audit of the IPC interface.

risk.why: Clients relying specifically on HTTP 403 status codes rather than JSON-RPC error payloads for JSON-RPC 2.0 or batch denials may misparse responses.
